 Required Permits
  • Site Plan and Design Review (PL No. 25-0058) for development of a site greater than

  • Conditional Use Permit (CUP No. 25-01) for a drive-through restaurant subject to South
  Gate Municipal Code (SGMC) Sections 11.40.220 and 11.22.090(D).
  • Zone Change (ZC No. 25-01) to change the zone from NL to UN and remove the Corridor

  • General Plan Amendment (GPA No. 25-01) to change the land use designation from

RECOMMENDATION:
Staff recommends that the Planning Commission:

1. Find that in accordance with CEQA, this project qualifies for a categorical exemption under
  CEQA Guidelines Section 15303 (Class 3), “New Construction or Conversion of Small
  Structures,” and is thereby exempt from CEQA in that the proposed restaurant is less than
  2,500 square feet and located in an urbanized area.

2. Adopt Resolution No. 2026-01, included as Attachment 1, approving PL No. 25-0058 and CUP
  No. 25-01, and recommending to the City Council approval of ZC No. 25-01 and GPA No. 25-
  01 for the development of a site located at 4816 and 4820 Firestone Boulevard, and 8915
  Vossler Avenue.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION:
The project site has a vacant 3,680 SF restaurant building on the northwestern lot. The northeastern
and southern lots are developed as parking lots. The proposed project is for a speculative restaurant
pad in which the applicant is actively seeking a tenant. The proposed restaurant does not include
indoor dining, but will provide a drive-through lane and a walk-up window. The drive-through
lane can accommodate nine cars with a length of more than 170 feet of queuing from the entrance
to the pick-up window. The applicant intends to keep and reface the existing pole sign along
Firestone Boulevard.

There is a 15-foot-wide public alley between the two northern properties along Firestone
Boulevard and the southern property at 8915 Vossler Avenue. The alley will continue to be
maintained by the City. It allows access to the southern parking lot and to the restaurant’s drive-
through lane.

Landscaping will be provided throughout the project site, including along the streets and in the
parking lot. A trash enclosure is proposed on the east side of the southern lot next to the handicap
parking space. An electric vehicle parking space is proposed in the southeastern corner.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS:
Under the California Environmental Quality Act (California Public Resources Code §§ 21000, et
seq., “CEQA”) and the regulations promulgated thereunder (14 California Code of Regulations §§
15000, et seq., the “CEQA Guidelines”), the project qualifies as a Class 3 Categorical Exemption
pursuant to Section 15303 (Class 3 – New Construction or Conversion of Small Structures) of the
CEQA Guidelines (Title 14, Chapter 3 of the California Code of Regulations). The Project will
not cause a significant effect on the environment and is, therefore, categorically exempt from the

  8
 requirement for the preparation of environmental documents under CEQA (see Attachment 2).

BACKGROUND:

Site History and Environmental Setting
The project site consists of three lots: one developed lot and two lots used for parking. The
developed lot (4816 Firestone Boulevard) at the northwestern portion of the site has a one-story,
3,680 SF commercial building built in 1928, which has been used as a restaurant.

The site is bounded by Firestone Boulevard to the north, Vossler Avenue to the east, residential
uses to the south, and commercial uses to the west. The Azalea Shopping Center is located north
of the site across Firestone Boulevard. Regional access is provided by Interstate 710 (I-710),
located approximately 0.69 miles to the east.

The entire site is flat with paved sidewalks along the streets. An alley traverses the site from the
east to the west. Vegetation is minimal, limited to a few street trees along Vossler Avenue and a
planter area at the northeastern corner. The southern parking lot has a planter area along Vossler
Avenue, which has not been maintained. There are no sensitive habitats or protected species in the
area. Wildlife consists of common urban birds and small mammals. There are no known historical,
cultural, or scenic designations on the property.

Site Characteristics: The subject site measures approximately 186 feet from Firestone Boulevard
to the southern property line, and 128 feet from Vossler Avenue to the western property line on
the southern lot. The three lots are all rectangular-shaped with an alley traversing the project site.

 ANALYSIS:

Required Findings for a CUP
Pursuant to SGMC Section 11.52.030, before a CUP may be granted, the Planning Commission
(or the City Council on appeal) shall make all the following findings, as applicable to the property:

  •  Approval of the CUP is consistent with and will not adversely affect the intent and purpose
  of this title or the city’s General Plan.

  •  The design and development of the land use and conditions of the CUP are compatible with
  the existing and future land uses of the applicable zone.

  •  Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to
  the character or function of the neighborhood.

The proposed Resolution supports the findings required under Section 11.52.030.

 Issues of Concern

Parking
Per Table 11.33-1 of SGMC Section 11.33.040, a food establishment less than 4,000 SF of floor
area is required to have 1 parking space per 100 SF of gross floor area. Gross floor area calculations
are based on the area within the surrounding exterior walls of a building or any portion thereof.
The new 1,700 SF building requires 17 parking spaces. The applicant is proposing 14 parking
spaces, including one ADA space and one electric vehicle (EV) space.

Pursuant to Assembly Bill 2097 (AB 2097), cities are prohibited from imposing minimum
automobile parking requirements for most new residential and commercial developments located
within one-half mile of a major transit stop. A major transit stop is located directly across Firestone
Boulevard, north of the project site, in front of the Azalea Shopping Center. In addition, a major
transit center is planned along Atlantic Avenue north of Firestone Boulevard, within a few hundred
feet of the subject property. Accordingly, the project qualifies for reduced on-site parking
requirements; nevertheless, it will provide 14 on-site parking spaces and accommodate up to 10
vehicles within the drive-through area.

Additionally, the proposed building will replace an existing 3,680 SF restaurant building that was
required to provide 37 parking spaces. There are 40 spaces currently provided; however, many of
the spaces are nonconforming in regard to size and location, and minimal landscaping, lighting,
and other improvements are provided. The proposed project would improve these conditions.

Design/Site Plan Review
Development on parcels smaller than 15,000 square feet is typically subject to administrative
review and does not require Planning Commission approval. However, because the project
includes a request for a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) for a drive-through, as well as a Zone
Change and General Plan Amendment—both of which require City Council approval—the project
is being processed as a single, consolidated application.

The applicant is proposing a modern building design with materials such as aluminum wall panels,
metal and wood trellis, smooth exterior plaster, sconces, and metal canopies. Exterior building
colors will be earth-toned and are described as “Arcadia black,” “raindrop,” and “good night.” A
covered outdoor patio will be located at the front of the building with chairs and tables. The trash
enclosure will be located in the rear parking lot and constructed of split-face block with a security
mesh, a roof covering, and a corrugated metal gate. A condition has been added to require a one-
foot-wide curb along the south side along the parking lot to allow passengers to exit a vehicle.

Exterior areas will be well-lit with lighting poles in the parking lot and along the alley. Sconces
and other lighting will be provided along the sides of the building. Additional lighting will be
provided from the interior of the building through glass doors and windows.

As the building currently has no tenant, signage will be reviewed by staff at a later time. Sample
signage is shown on the elevations and renderings. An existing pole sign is proposed to remain at
the front of the property along Firestone Boulevard. However, renderings appear to show the pole
replaced with a thicker pole with a much wider sign that encroaches over the sidewalk. Typically,
existing pole signs are allowed to remain but not be replaced. An alternative is to replace the pole
sign with a pedestrian-level monument sign, similar to those at Dunkin’ to the west and WSS to
the north. A condition has not been added, but the Commission does have discretion to require it.

 Landscaping includes various trees and shrubs along the perimeter and parking areas. The plant
palette includes strawberry trees, bottle trees, privet, lantana, purple sage, and other shrubs. New
landscaping will enhance the appearance of the property. A condition has been included that the
project meets the model water efficient landscape ordinance (MWELO) requirements.

Zone Change (ZC No. 25-01) and General Plan Amendment (GPA No. 25-01)
The applicant proposes a Zone Change to change the zone from NL to UN and remove the Corridor
Transition Overlay, and a General Plan Amendment to change the land use designation from
Medium Density Residential to Commercial for the property at 8915 Vossler Avenue. The UN
zoning district will be consistent with the zoning for the restaurant properties (4816 and 4820
Firestone Boulevard) as well as other properties along the south side of Firestone Boulevard, which
are also zoned UN. The Planning Commission is a recommending body in this instance and will
make a recommendation to the City Council for final action. A condition is included to require the
southern lot at 8915 Vossler Avenue to be linked in perpetuity to the northern lots to prevent it
from being sold separately, potentially eliminating much of the parking.

The proposed Zone Change and General Plan Amendment are appropriate, as the property at 8915
Vossler Avenue has historically been used as a parking lot serving adjacent commercial uses. In
addition, the proposed UN zoning designation permits residential development at densities of up
to 40 dwelling units per acre, compared to the 9-16 dwelling units per acre allowed under the
Medium Density Residential land use designation. Accordingly, the Zone Change is consistent
with the City’s Housing Element and would not result in a loss of housing opportunity; rather, it

  CEQA Guidelines in December 2018 which now identify Vehicle Miles Traveled (VMT) as the most
  appropriate metric to evaluate a project's transportation impact under CEQA (§ 15064.3).

  delay, roadway capacity and congestion, generally will no longer constitute a significant environmental
  impact.

  retail projects with less than 50,000 square feet of area are screened out from requiring a full VMT
  analysis. A copy of the guidelines is contained in Attachment B.
